summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop system using Charmbracelet/Bubbletea libraries, covering all management operations (activate, suppress, archive, promote, add) across 4 tabs: Memories, Injection, History, Settings.
summary.outcome: The TUI was scaffolded and implemented with all 4 tabs, but the session ended mid-polish — borders were still not rendering visibly and spacing issues remained unresolved across multiple iteration rounds.

repo: The project uses a package-per-feature structure under cmd/entire/cli/ (e.g., memoryloop/, insights/, settings/) — new TUI package follows this as memorylooptui/
The docs/superpowers/ directory is gitignored — brainstorm specs and plans written there are not tracked
ACCESSIBLE=1 env var is an established pattern for disabling TUI and falling back to plain-text output
termstyle package provides the shared color palette and NO_COLOR handling; TUI must use it for consistency
Memory loop state lives in .entire/memory-loop.json; requires 'entire memory-loop refresh' to populate before TUI has data to show

code.finding: Initial accent color was set to cyan (ANSI 6); changed to orange (ANSI 214). Inactive tab color was dark gray (8) which is invisible on dark terminals — must use at least 245 for visibility.
Lipgloss border color '8' (dark gray) is invisible on dark terminals; '245' (light gray) is required for visible borders. Border width must be set relative to m.width or it renders incorrectly.
maxWidth cap was set to 80, making the layout too narrow; increased to 120. Tab content delegation requires careful ordering — global key handling must not swallow keys intended for child models.
Settings key handling (m/p/+/-) was suspected to fail due to value receiver state propagation issue with settingsChangedMsg — pointer receivers required for mutable tab models.
Same border color issue as tab_memories — hardcoded cyan '6' in table selected row needed replacing with orange style variable.

workflow: Brainstorming skill + visual companion (localhost HTML server) was effective for iterating on layout decisions before writing any code
Subagent-driven development dispatched implementers per task group — Tasks 1-3 were batched as tightly coupled foundational work
Fix agents committed their own changes, so checking 'git log' after agent return is necessary to know what's already committed vs. still staged
Lipgloss v1 API is in use — context7 docs lookup was needed to verify border API correctness
gomod lint errors on uncommitted go.mod changes are expected noise during development and not real failures

friction: Border rendering was the persistent blocker — multiple rounds of fixes (border color too dark, width not set, lipgloss API uncertainty) without full resolution by session end
Visual companion server shut down between sessions and had to be restarted manually with content re-written
Fix agents committed changes silently, requiring a git log check to understand what was already committed vs. what remained
maxWidth=80 cap was an invisible constraint that made the layout look broken on normal terminals
Detail pane was hidden by default (required Enter) instead of showing immediately — not caught until user saw the real TUI
open_items: Borders still not visible on Memories detail card and Injection match results at session end — root cause (lipgloss width calculation) not fully resolved
Spacing between top tabs and filter bar, and between memory list and detail card, still needs adjustment
History tab 'R' refresh trigger is a placeholder — async refresh wiring not implemented
Prompt injection tester on Injection tab doesn't appear to work correctly (reported by user)
Settings tab key handling (m/p/+/-) was reportedly not working — fix was attempted but not confirmed working
No tests written for the TUI package — plan explicitly deferred this to manual verification
Injection log detail card (bottom card for selected log entry) was partially implemented but not confirmed working
prune action keybinding (D) was added late in spec review — may not be fully wired through
